For Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) internet access, the primary protocols used are:

## **GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network)**
- Most common protocol worldwide
- Provides up to 2.5 Gbps downstream / 1.25 Gbps upstream
- Uses ITU-T G.984 standard
- Shared bandwidth among multiple users (typically 32-64)

## **EPON (Ethernet Passive Optical Network)**
- Popular in Asia, especially Japan
- Based on IEEE 802.3ah standard
- 1 Gbps symmetrical bandwidth
- Uses Ethernet frames natively

## **XG-PON/XGS-PON**
- Next-generation GPON
- XG-PON: 10 Gbps down / 2.5 Gbps up
- XGS-PON: 10 Gbps symmetrical
- ITU-T G.987 standard

## **Active Ethernet (Point-to-Point)**
- Dedicated fiber for each customer
- Can provide up to 10 Gbps or more
- More expensive but offers guaranteed bandwidth
- Common in business and some residential deployments

The choice of protocol depends on:
- Regional preferences
- ISP infrastructure
- Cost considerations
- Required bandwidth
- Number of subscribers

GPON remains the most widely deployed protocol globally due to its cost-effectiveness and mature technology.
